name: MVTec AD
ability_definition: The ability to see details at close range (within a few feet of the observer).

task_realism.reasoning: Visual inspection of manufactured items for scratches, dents, contamination, and structural flaws is a real workplace task that depends heavily on near vision. Quality inspectors, assemblers, and machine operators do this kind of close-range detail detection. The tasks are realistic but limited to one occupational context.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Images are high-resolution close-ups under controlled lighting, with mostly centered and aligned objects. The model trains on defect-free samples of each category. Real inspection involves variable lighting, orientation, occlusion, and throughput pressure. It also involves handling or repositioning parts to view them from different angles. Real work has class drift and unfamiliar defect types that the curated split only partly captures.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only one slice of near vision: spotting surface and structural anomalies across 15 object and texture categories. It omits reading fine print, reading gauges and small labels, judging fine color or alignment for precision assembly, and visually guiding fine manipulation. It also excludes near-field depth perception. The unsupervised novelty-detection setup further narrows what is measured to deviation-from-normal, rather than general detail resolution.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are genuine photographs of real industrial parts and materials. Outputs are image-level anomaly scores and pixel-level defect maps, which resemble what automated optical inspection systems produce in practice. There is no forced multiple choice. However, it lacks the pass/fail decisions tied to tolerances and the defect-category reporting that human inspectors produce.

transferability_reasoning: MVTec AD uses authentic close-range industrial imagery where success depends on noticing small visual flaws, so it transfers reasonably well to inspection-oriented uses of near vision. Its controlled capture conditions limit how much it reflects the broader ability. So does its narrow focus on surface anomaly detection, which leaves out reading, fine assembly, and other near-vision work, making it a moderate proxy.

2020.metric: Mean image-level AUROC (%) across the 15 MVTec AD categories
2020.human_reference: Relevant workforce: industrial visual inspectors and quality-control workers with normal near vision who judge close-up product images for defects (median inspector, not an expert metrologist).

2021.metric: mean image-level AUROC (%) across 15 MVTec AD categories
2021.human_reference: Relevant specialist workforce: industrial visual quality inspectors examining close-up product images for surface and structural defects
